newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower on overbought status.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower on overbought status.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures echoed their CBOT counterparts, breaking late and ending lower on perceptions the market was overbought, traders said.
"When a market's extremely overbought, it can turn on a dime, and that's what we saw today," a trader said. "Chicago broke late, and Kansas City followed in panic-type selling."

Traders said KCBT wheat did not break as hard as CBOT wheat because of strength in the December/March spread. The spread widened on the day and was offered late at 40-1/2 cents, compared its closing level Wednesday of 38-1/4 cents.
"We saw a lack of buy orders late in the day -- it felt like we were trading world values by the end of the session... instead of domestic ones," a KCBT trader said.
KCBT wheat closed 1-1/2 cents per bushel lower to one cent higher, with December down 3/4 cent at $4.40 -- its intraday low. March lost 1-1/4 cents to close at $4.01.
Until the last hour of trade, KCBT wheat had been higher as shorts tried to buy their way out of the December contract on concerns about dwindling stocks of deliverable-grade wheat.
Traders said CIS bull-spread two million Dec/March bushels at between 38 and 40 cents.
Man International bear-spread one million March/Dec at 40 to 41 cents and FIMAT bear-spread 1.1 million March/Dec at 40 to 42-1/2 cents, traders said.
CIS sold 1.9 million March and bought one million Dec. Benson-Quinn sold 1.2 million March. Man International also bought 1.2 million Dec and 1.3 million March.
Traders said KCBT wheat drew light pressure after the EU granted export licenses for 311,200 tonnes of wheat at a refund of 16.50 Ecus per tonne, up slightly from 15.97 Ecus last week.
